correctness.rationale: Octagonal P-angle reduces to Q(A,B)=A²+B²−(√2−1)AB−4≤0 for all unit boundary pairs. Dihedral symmetry fixes x on one edge. For all eight y edges, eight support choices for A and for B, the exact Q(√2) algorithm intersects supporting halfspaces, generates 126 nonempty active-support cells, checks 176 cell vertices and finds maximal Q=0; convexity on each cell supplies the continuum inequality. The independent reconstruction executed the inspected code algorithm and reproduced 126/176/max=0 and adjacent-vertex witness A=2,B=2(√2−1). The source code for the finite reduction was fully inspected; the local verifier reproduction is algorithmically equivalent, not byte-for-byte the frozen blob.
residual_risks: Finite exact enumeration depends on exhaustive dihedral and active-support partitions; verified loops show complete facet and edge coverage. Numerical floats were not used.

checked_sources: Yang–Li, New Geometric Constant Related to the P-angle Function in Banach Spaces, arXiv:2208.11239v1
value.rationale: The Yang–Li P-angle is a natural Banach-space geometric invariant, and the regular octagon is a canonical non-Hilbert polyhedral test space. The exact sharp value requires a genuine all-unit-pair optimization (126 active-support polyhedral cells), separates this invariant from previously known octagon vNJ/angle-modulus values, and includes a sharp geometric maximizing pair. The result is a useful exact benchmark not mechanically implied by checked constants.
residual_risks: The result is one planar norm, not a theorem for all polygons; a general encompassing profile could make it redundant.
